ai.description: This gecko reaches 50 mm SVL. It is grey-brown with dark dorsal spots and a pale belly. Key features include a slender body, granular scales, and a tail with distinct transverse rows of tubercles.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Hemidactylus gracilis* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, dark-edged, pale vertebral stripe running down the center of its back, which is absent in similar species.
ai.habitat: *Hemidactylus gracilis* inhabits dry deciduous forests and scrublands in the Indian subcontinent, typically found at low to moderate elevations on tree trunks or rocks.
ai.behavior: The Graceful Leaf-toed Gecko is primarily nocturnal, actively hunting small insects on tree trunks and rocky surfaces under the cover of darkness.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hemidactylus gracilis* is oviparous, laying a clutch of two hard-shelled, spherical eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, from June to September.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Hemidactylus gracilis* is endemic to peninsular India, primarily occurring in the dry deciduous forests and rocky scrublands of Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, and Karnataka.
